nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: NF was ultrasonicated in 3.0 mol L⁻¹ HCl solution, deionized (DI) water, and ethanol for 10 min, respectively, to remove the surface oxides and residues.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiₓSᵧ Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.2 mmol CTAB and 5 mL of hydrazine hydrate were dissolved in 60 mL of DI water. After transferring the above solution into a 100-mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave containing 4.4 mmol sulfur powder and a piece of NF (2.0 × 3.0 cm²), the autoclave was maintained at 160 °C for 12 h. Finally, NiₓSᵧ/NF was obtained after being washed and dried.

nodes.name: Anodic Electrodeposition MnOₓHᵧ
nodes.procedure: NiₓSᵧ@MnOₓHᵧ/NF was synthesized through a simple electrodeposition process in a three-electrode system, consisting of the NiₓSᵧ/NF as the working electrode, a Pt wire as the counter electrode, and a saturated calomel electrode as the reference electrode. The anodic galvanostatic electrodeposition was conducted at 0.5 mA cm⁻² for different time (optimized at 150 s) in 50 mL of electrolyte containing 7.5 mmol MnSO₄·H₂O and 15.0 mmol CH₃COONa. After the electrodeposition process, NiₓSᵧ@MnOₓHᵧ/NF was prepared after being rinsed and dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: 3D NixSy nanorods with diameter 100-400 nm grown on NF surface; after electrodeposition, entire surfaces covered with MnOxHy nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a-c, 3D Ni_x S_y nanorods were in situ grown successfully on the surface of NF... Their high-magnifed SEM images manifest that these nanorods possess a diameter of about 100–400 nm with relatively smooth surfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanorod structure of NixSy and NixSy@MnOxHy; clear interface observed between NixSy core and MnOxHy shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figs. 2g–h and k–l present the nanorod structure of Ni_x S_y and Ni_x S_y @ MnO_x H_y, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NixSy shows interplanar spacing 0.24 nm corresponding to (003) Ni3S2 and (220) NiS; clear core-shell interface with crystalline MnOxHy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (Fig. 2i–j) of Ni_x S_y nanorod demonstrate an interplanar spacing of 0.24 nm, corresponding to the (003) plane of Ni3S2 and (220) plane of NiS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous spatial distribution of Ni, S, Mn, O throughout NixSy@MnOxHy nanorod; Mn/Ni molar ratio 1:40.3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S4 shows the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and corresponding energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum of Ni_x S_y @ MnO_x H_y nanorod... the Mn/Ni molar ratio is 1:40.3.

nodes.characterization_summary: NixSy/NF and NixSy@MnOxHy/NF show peaks matching Ni3S2 (PDF#44-1418) and NiS (PDF#12-0041); no MnOxHy peaks observed due to low mass loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The other peaks of Ni_x S_y / NF and Ni_x S_y @ MnO_x H_y / NF match well with those of Ni3S2 (PDF#44–1418) and NiS (PDF#12–0041).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 peaks at 852.5 eV (Ni-Ni in Ni3S2), 855.6 eV (Ni-S) shifts positively to 855.8 eV in NixSy@MnOxHy/NF indicating electron transfer; S 2p shows S2- (161.1/162.3 eV), S2^2- (162.0/163.2 eV), S-O (168.4 eV); Mn 2p3/2 shows Mn2+ (640.6 eV), Mn3+ (641.8 eV), Mn4+ (643.19 eV); O 1s shows Mn-O (529.6 eV), -OH (531.0 eV), -OOH (531.8 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3b, regarding Ni 2p XPS spectra... the Ni 2p3/2 peak located at 852.5 eV is attributed to the Ni–Ni bonds in Ni3S2... the second peak of Ni 2p3/2 positively shifts from 855.6 to 855.8 eV... For Mn 2p3/2 (Fig. 3d), three peaks of MnOxHy/NF appear at 640.6, 641.8, and 643.19 eV., which are assigned to Mn2+, Mn3+, and Mn4+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shows oxidized Ni, decreased Ni-S coordination number; S K-edge pre-edge shifts to higher energy; Mn K-edge average valence <+4; FT-EXAFS shows Mn-S at 1.9 Å, Ni-S at 1.7 Å, Ni-Ni at 2.0 Å, confirming abundant Mn-S bonds at interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Mn K-edge FT‐EXAFS... an obvious Mn–S peak appears at 1.9 Å for Ni_x S_y @ MnO_x H_y / NF, further confirming the existence of Mn–S bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms almost no Ni dissolution in electrolyte after stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Then, the Ni content of the electrolyte after the stability measurement was detected by ICP‐MS, and the corresponding result indicates almost no Ni content exits in the electrolyte.
